newsitem.title: USA: CompuServe Chief Executive Massey resigns.
newsitem.headline: CompuServe Chief Executive Massey resigns.

text.p: CompuServe Corp. said Monday its President and Chief Executive Officer Robert Massey, resigned effective immediately.
The world's second largest online service said Massey's duties will be assumed on an interim basis by Chairman Frank Salizzoni.
Salizzoni is also president and chief executive of tax preparation firm H&R Block Inc., which owns about 80 percent of CompuServe.

"We respect Bob's desire to pursue other interests and thank him for his years of service to CompuServe," Salizzoni said. "Our goal remains a speedy and sustained turnaround at CompuServe, and under Bob's leadership, the company has made progress in that direction. The board of directors will work quickly to find a chief executive who will continue the process."
A search is underway for a replacement for Massey, according to Salizzoni. Until then, Salizzoni will divide his time between CompuServe and H&R Block.
Massey, 50, who joined CompuServe in 1976, became president and CEO in June 1995. Prior to that, he served as the company's executive vice president of the Network Services division.
CompuServe has been hit by competition among online services and Internet providers.
In its second fiscal quarter ended Oct. 31, Compuserv reported a loss of $58 million, or 63 cents per share, vs. a year earlier profit of $14 million, or 19 cents a share.
"We are financially stronger today than just a few months ago and that was some of the progress made under Bob's (Massey's) leadership," a spokesman said.

"It's been a really challenging past year because of all the changes in the marketplce and I know that Bob has been putting in mega hours ... he decided that at this point he just wants to make a change."
